newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bond spreads hold, Ohio Ed stems drop.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bond spreads hold, Ohio Ed stems drop.

text.p: U.S. corporate high-grade bonds held spreads at mid-session as prices eroded with U.S. Treasuries, unfazed by the promise of hefty supply in coming weeks, traders said.
Meanwhile, Ohio Edison debt made a mild recovery from wider markets on Monday after the company said it will merge with Centerior Energy in a $1.61 billion stock swap deal.

Ohio Edison's 7-7/8 percent debt of 2024 traded at a spread of 155 basis points on Tuesday morning, one trader said, compared with a late Monday offer of 160. The debt widened more than 30 basis points on Monday.

Centerior debt, which tightened 40 to 50 basis points on the merger news, traded in the middle of wide 225 bid, 200 offer quotes seen late on Monday. One trader said bonds changed hands at 215 on Tuesday morning.

In other action, traders said the market has been busied with especially active banking sector issuance, including a $200 million Bank of Boston issue on Monday and $70 million KeyBank of Oregon and $250 million Suntrust Bank issues on Tuesday.
"Secondary levels have held in fairly well today," one bank and finance trader said.
"I've been telling people for two weeks they should be worried about supply, but spreads tightened in, yesterday they widened one to two basis points and we're holding those levels fine today."

New issues came tight, dealers said, but were quickly knocked down to "more realistic" levels. Bank of Boston's 10-year notes, priced at a 65 basis point spread on Monday, were quoted at 70 bid, 68 offer at midday.
Further, Nationsbank's mega $1.4 billion offering of five-, 10- and 20-year debt is slated to come as early as Tuesday, dealers said.
Topping new issuance on Tuesday, SunTrust Bank issued $250 million 10-year subordinated notes with a 7.25 percent coupon priced to yield 48.5 basis points over 10-year Treasuries.

Traders said prices in general were under pressure after comments from a senior Federal Reserve official suggested a 25 basis point fed funds rate hike was imminent. In an interview with Reuters, the official said eight of twelve member banks had submitted discount rate hike requests and three of those favored a 50 basis point discount rate hike.
The 30-year Treasury bond was quoted down 18/32 at 96-30/32 to yield 6.99 percent at 1308 EDT/1708 GMT.
